findings.reproduction: At 8040797, run cargo test --locked on Windows MSVC.
findings.expected: Both wiping fixtures compile on every supported native platform.
findings.observed: Windows CI reports E0063 twice at standard_input.rs:229 and :243.

findings.recommendedFix: Create fixtures through StandardInput::new and set the same bytes/ranges.

findings.title: Unrelated smaps prefix ordering can refuse concurrent native C calls
findings.reproduction: Run the concurrent_c_calls_keep_verified_work_area_protection regression on the former parser.
findings.expected: Every owned page requires exact dump-exclusion coverage; unrelated prefix records do not refuse that coverage.
findings.observed: Actual C concurrency returned MemoryProtection; diagnostic booleans locate the overlapping record wholly before the owned range, before any owned coverage. The minimized deterministic fixture also fails before the fix.
findings.impact: A valid concurrent operation may fail closed. No wrong cryptographic output or exposed work area was demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Track strict progress over owned pages without imposing global prefix ordering.
findings.requiredVerification: Deterministic red/green, unchanged missing-dd/gap/owned-overlap/I/O/budget refusals, concurrent actual C calls and independent known answers.
findings.implementedFix: covered_owned_pages gates the monotonic-coverage rule; all owned-page checks and finite read bounds remain.

findings.title: Follow-up: hosted macOS lacks authorization for the unprotected PT_ATTACH control
findings.reproduction: At 8040797, run the macOS portable job without an authorized public probe monitor.
findings.expected: A successful attach/stop/detach control precedes the protected child signal assertion.
findings.observed: The control returns EPERM and the paired test correctly fails UNAVAILABLE; this does not verify target hardening.
findings.impact: The required macOS native acceptance gate cannot establish its positive precondition.
findings.recommendedFix: Explicitly authorize only the fixed public-data monitor and its named probe children in hosted CI.
findings.requiredVerification: Real native control success and protected SIGSEGV, exact one-test/completion markers, unchanged production privilege behavior.
findings.implementedFix: An explicit test-only opt-in invokes /usr/bin/sudo -n for the fixed monitor; actual child signals are checked inside it, before sudo result relay. No OS policy is changed.

record.kind: Read-only scoped macOS hosted-CI capability diagnosis and recommendation, not fix acceptance
record.observed: Native macOS library tests429passed; CLI204passed1failed8ignored. The unrestricted public PT_ATTACH control returned -1/EPERM, so the outer enforcement test correctly refused to certify protection. The protected branch was not established by this run.
record.inference: An environment authorization restriction is consistent with EPERM and the XNU authorization path, but this log does not identify the exact MAC/authorization policy and does not establish a production hardening regression.
recommendedSeam: Keep the normal cargo build/test suite unprivileged. Enable an explicit macOS-CI test-only opt-in for the public paired probe only.

A local macOS test wrapper may execute /usr/bin/sudo -n -- followed by the absolute current test executable and one hardcoded exact ignored privileged-monitor test. Do not accept a caller-selected binary, arbitrary test name, shell command or free-form environment command.

The root public monitor should run the existing actual unrestricted and protected tracer children through the same current executable. Check the unrestricted PT_ATTACH success, stopped-child observation, PT_DETACH success and attached marker first. Check actual protected tracer ExitStatus.signal()==SIGSEGV inside the monitor. Require monitor success, a unique completion marker and exact one-test success in the unprivileged caller.
This avoids depending on whether sudo relays a signalled command as a signal or exit139. The generic process-test runner need not be widened; a small local wrapper plus monitor is sufficient.

Do not fall back on EPERM, skip, PT_TRACE_ME substitution, weakened marker/status assertions or accepting protected refusal alone. sudo authorization failure or another failed positive control must remain a failed/unavailable test.

Use stdin null, public fixed inputs only, core limit0 in intentionally signalled children, bounded ready/attach/cleanup stages and ownership of all children. Preserve the existing target lifetime/reparenting escape; consider a marker after target READY just before PT_ATTACH to make unrelated earlier SIGSEGV less plausible.

No sudo -E, root Cargo invocation, DevToolsSecurity/System Integrity Protection changes or production privilege behavior is needed. Apply opt-in only in the macOS CI test command and document its public-fixture scope.
risksAndLimits: Passwordless sudo exists on documented GitHub-hosted macOS runners, but root is not proof that every MAC policy permits attach. The actual same-mode positive control remains decisive.

Running checkout-built code as root is a real privilege boundary. Keep it explicitly authorized and confined to named public test processes on the ephemeral hosted runner. This is not protection against a malicious checkout or a claim that privilege is harmless.

Root tracer death bypasses its Rust Drop implementation. Verify target exit through reparenting/deadline and drain/close inherited pipes so failure cannot leave root orphans or hang output collection.

A get-task-allow/debugger entitlement approach changes test Mach-O signatures/identities and still needs an actual PT_ATTACH positive control. Task-port documentation is not proof that it fixes raw ptrace authorization. A debugger entitlement can request an interactive administrator authorization, unsuitable as an assumed unattended fix.
Keep any development/debug entitlements out of shipping release binaries. Existing hardened-runtime inspection and direct PT_DENY_ATTACH enforcement are separate guarantees.
No implementation, build, runtime probe or macOS execution was performed by this reviewer. The recommendation requires native hosted-CI validation and independent review of the implemented delta.

invariantAssessment.invariant: Admission owns the entire requested page extent
invariantAssessment.reason: WorkArea retains page-aligned/page-rounded Layout, checked end and logical C extent. Its zeroed allocation owner exists before fallible madvise/readback; refusal drops that owner before any Argon2 use. Public MemoryProtection error propagation, cleanup and cryptographic parameters are unchanged.

invariantAssessment.invariant: Irrelevant prefix cannot provide owned protection evidence
invariantAssessment.reason: Before coverage, cursor remains the allocation start. VmFlags records ending at/before cursor are discarded and cannot advance it. Prefix headers can repeat or move relative to earlier irrelevant headers, but their flags cannot make owned pages pass. A pending header covering cursor cannot be overwritten before its VmFlags.

invariantAssessment.invariant: Owned coverage is complete, disjoint and dd protected
invariantAssessment.reason: A relevant VmFlags record needs first<=cursor<last and the exact dd whitespace token. Progress strictly increases cursor, bounded by self.end. After the first progress, headers with first<cursor refuse; a header with first>cursor later fails the gap check. Therefore each subsequent admitted extent starts exactly at cursor and no missing/overlapping owned span is accepted. Completion requires cursor==end.

Stray/missing flags, malformed/inverted/overflowing headers, EOF/no LF, missing exact dd, relevant overlap and gaps still refuse. I/O errors propagate and require converts them to the typed protection refusal. The whole underlying read remains bounded8MiB and each line8KiB; there is no unbounded retry or new global state.

invariantAssessment.invariant: No API or WASM regression from parser path
invariantAssessment.reason: engine::dump_protection remains cfg(target_os="linux"), ffi native-only, and the new real-C test is Linux-only. No public signature, error-code change, KDF/format change, dependency or browser path is introduced.

testAssessment.deterministic: The new duplicated entirely-before-owner prefix fixture is red on the exact reversed rule and green after the fix. Its paired missing-owned-dd case remains false. It specifically checks the observed false refusal while retaining a nonvacuous protection oracle.
testAssessment.negativeControls: The existing own-range overlap, gap, missing-flags, ddd, malformed-header, truncation, bounded-read and I/O cases are byte-preserved and pass.
testAssessment.concurrentAllocation: Four threads each allocate128 separate512KiB-plus-variable-page areas and require successful protection and wiped contents. This is a bounded stress control, not proof of every interleaving.
testAssessment.actualC: Four threads each perform64 RFC9106 32KiB C calls and compare actual tags to RustCrypto. The same body failed with MemoryProtection on baseline and passed20 retained executions on the corrected parser. The existing160 deterministic public C/RustCrypto parameter cases also pass.
testAssessment.runtimeAccepted: Main-owned linux-policy-green runs four parser/allocation tests,20 real-C stress executions and the existing160-case comparison; receipt exits0/sourceunchanged. No independent runtime repetition by reviewer.

officialDocumentation.summary: The official proc documentation says partial maps/smaps reads race with modifications, yet still documents monotonically advancing nonoverlapping regions. Thus it does not justify claiming duplicate prefix VMAs are generally guaranteed or permitted. The patch limits parser relevance to owned pages regardless of the observed prefix anomaly; no kernel bug mechanism is proven.

limitations: This fixes the demonstrated unrelated-prefix false refusal and retains owned-span fail-closed rules; bounded stress does not establish every scheduling case.
A fragmented/anomalous stream within the owned span, missing procfs metadata or the configured scan limits may still refuse safely.
Readback establishes policy at admission, not a permanent security lock against another privileged actor changing pages later.
No actual core-dump secret recovery experiment or universal kernel behavior claim is made.
Current fast gates/hosted platform CI are independent required coordinator checks; this review does not relabel pending runs as green.
Current SECURITY claims remain the same: dd on every owned page, bounded readback, procfs requirement and allocator/privileged-change limits.
Windows fixture and macOS test-monitor behavior are outside this reviewer's semantic acceptance.
